matches.mechanism: Changing the expert implementation and its treatment of routed matrices may reduce GEMM and staging costs. Backend activation and grouped-versus-indexed selection require separate contrasts to identify which change matters.

Implementation evidence: #62463 exposes direct paged candidate scoring with compact logits and device-side causal-bound preparation; #62000 exposes candidate-K gathering and default-off controls. Both avoid full compressed-context scoring for consumers. Transfer inference: direct reads may additionally avoid gather workspace traffic and fixed copy cost. Benefits depend on actual indexer shapes and context-to-candidate width, not TP-local attention-head padding.

Affected-event frequency: learned-router calls meeting actual weight/activation dtype, shape, padded-row and dispatch predicates; exclude bypasses and unaffected small-row calls. Component occupied time: eligible GEMM plus casts and dispatch overhead. Exposed time: its contribution to the target or draft dependency chain, without summing ranks as wall time. Expected net saving: measured exposed per-call reduction weighted by native calls, minus conversion, warmup and resource-contention costs. Service transfer: routing arithmetic can alter subsequent expert work, so local kernel speed and quality must be checked before the frozen service test.
